claim: Forwarded-clock D-PHY transfers one data bit on each clock edge: lane bit rate R_lane = 2*f_DDR and byte rate = R_lane/8.
qualification: Applies to the forwarded-clock mode; newer embedded-clock D-PHY modes need a different model.

claim: Current D-PHY includes optional embedded clocking from v3.5; the overview is not proof that a 2018 handset uses it.
HS uses terminated differential signaling; LP uses unterminated single-ended signaling. A received emission mixture may include both states.
qualification: The mixture statement is an inference; signal-state identification requires measurement.

claim: DSI video mode streams timed pixel data; command mode can write a local frame buffer. Burst video shortens transfer time within a line.

evidence.locator: section 4.2, PDF 24 / printed 12; section 8.11, PDF 88-91 / printed 76-79

claim: DSI byte distribution is round-robin across lanes; RGB888 uses three successive component bytes. Four lanes therefore do not map to four fixed colors.

evidence.locator: section 6, PDF 31-33 / printed 19-21; section 8.8.23, PDF 77 / printed 65

qualification: The resulting lane/color cycle is derived from these two rules; packet headers and command bytes set its phase.

claim: Short packets have 4 bytes; long packets have a 4-byte header, payload, and 2-byte footer. Multiple packets can share a single HS transmission.
0x3e is the RGB888 video pixel-stream data type. 0x39 is DCS Long Write and includes a command byte before parameters/data.

evidence.locator: section 8.8.9.3, PDF 66 / printed 54; section 8.8.23, PDF 77 / printed 65

qualification: Command-mode image transport cannot be decoded by assuming every pixel packet is type 0x3e.

claim: A command-mode display has local refresh timing; TE can report timing events to the host. Link activity and panel scanning are distinct processes.
qualification: An actual phone may use a separate TE pin; this source describes DSI in-band TE. A periodic capture alone cannot identify either path.

claim: Driver and interconnect imbalance creates time-varying common-mode currents; connector skew can raise radiated emissions.
qualification: This does not establish the dominant source in any of the user captures.

claim: D-PHY compliance characterization explicitly measures static common-mode mismatch and dynamic common-mode variation in two frequency regions.
qualification: Test existence is not a measured common-mode spectrum for the target handset.

claim: Galaxy A7 (2018) has a 6.0-inch 1080 by 2220 Super AMOLED display.
qualification: An LCD-specific source/column-driver model is not automatically applicable to AMOLED.

claim: The pinned A7 kernel panel configuration selects s6e3fa7, MIPI command mode, 60 Hz, 4 data lanes, DSC disabled, and MIC disabled.
qualification: Not a measurement or a verified firmware configuration of the user device.

claim: A7 source requests dsi-hs-clk=997 and PLL P/M/S=3/230/1. The driver sets fin=26 MHz and divides hs_clk by 8 for byte clock.

evidence.locator: panel lines 57-59; dsim_reg.c lines 1341-1382; dsim_drv.c lines 1239-1246

qualification: This hs_clk variable is the full-rate internal clock/rate representation, not the half-rate forwarded clock.

claim: With the source PLL formula and ideal 26 MHz reference, R_lane=996.6666667 Mb/s, f_DDR=498.3333333 MHz, byte rate=124.5833333 MHz.
qualification: Driver integer arithmetic reports hs_clk=996 and byte_clk=124; requested 997, integer log, and ideal physical PLL frequency are different. The PLL-stable bootloader branch can skip reprogramming.

claim: At full-frame 60 Hz RGB888 updates, active payload is 3.452544 Gb/s total or 863.136 Mb/s per lane for four lanes; active pixel throughput is 143.856 Mpixel/s.

evidence.locator: 60 Hz and 4 lanes; dsim_reg.c line 1240 RGB24

qualification: Average full-frame payload demand. Excludes packet/state overhead; command update rate can differ from panel refresh.

claim: fc >> modulation bandwidth permits a complex-envelope description. It does not imply the RF carrier is the pixel clock or that the envelope bandwidth equals fh or fv.
qualification: fc must identify an observed RF component. Image-dependent payload and burst transitions can occupy much wider bandwidth than row/frame repetition rates.

claim: Small AM/PM around a nonzero coherent carrier can be linearized as u(t)≈A0[1+a(t)+j*phi(t)]. Carrier strength, smallness, and phase stability must be checked.
qualification: D-PHY does not mandate small-index AM/PM radiation. This is a testable local RF model, invalid near envelope zeros or for strong multicomponent interference.

claim: Common-mode origin does not guarantee low matrix rank. Repeated vertical stripes can themselves form a rank-one row-repeated matrix.
qualification: Rank is defined after choosing a matrix construction and window. MIPI target versus panel clutter cannot be assigned by rank alone.

claim: Residual CFO produces phase increments 2*pi*Delta_f*T_row between rows and 2*pi*Delta_f*T_frame between frames; timing mismatch changes raster alignment.
qualification: These mechanisms can create hue bands and gradients; source attribution needs controls and independent channels.

claim: Samples per pixel in a uniform raster model are Fs/fp. During uncompressed multi-lane payload, mean pixel time is b/(N*R_lane), so effective samples/pixel are Fs*b/(N*R_lane).

evidence.locator: lane mapping section 6 and format section 8.8.23

qualification: The latter is an average transport budget, not an isolated pixel sample. Packet overhead, lane superposition, command gating, receive bandwidth, and resampling all matter.

claim: The DSI term Common Mode fault describes a transmitter/receiver HS-versus-LP state mismatch, not ordinary common-mode electromagnetic radiation.
qualification: Avoid conflating this recovery/error term with the research target i_CM or V_CM.

claim: Null packets can keep lanes in HS while carrying dummy bytes; blanking packets carry timing and may carry arbitrary payload. HS activity duration is therefore not necessarily active-image payload duration.
qualification: The last sentence is an inference for burst segmentation. Actual use is implementation dependent.

claim: In this DSI revision, peripheral-to-host transfers use LP mode on data lane 0; other lanes are unidirectional.
qualification: Bidirectional LP control traffic should not be modeled as reverse high-speed RGB payload.

claim: RGB666 packed format aligns four pixels to nine bytes; loosely packed RGB666 spends three bytes per pixel with component bits in byte bits 7:2.

evidence.locator: sections 8.8.21-8.8.22, PDF 74-76 / printed 62-64; Figures 36-37 visually reviewed

qualification: Image bit depth alone does not determine wire bits per pixel. Confirm selected transport packing before sampling calculations.

claim: DSI header ECC protects 24 header data bits using six relevant parity bits; long-packet payload CRC detects errors and does not correct them.

evidence.locator: sections 9.1-9.6, PDF 95-101 / printed 83-89; Table 25 visually reviewed

qualification: P6/P7 are unused in DSI. Informative D24-D63 rows in the larger parity table must not be mistaken for this header payload. ECC/CRC cannot restore arbitrary bandwidth-limited analog IQ.

claim: DSC transport needs its compression mode, PPS and slice configuration. PPS changes take effect after the next vertical sync in video mode or signaled tearing effect in command mode.

evidence.locator: sections 8.8.25-8.8.26, PDF 79-80; Annex D.1.6, PDF 118-119 / printed 106-107

qualification: This is the v1.3 DSC profile, not all later DSC versions. The inspected A7 source has DSC disabled.

claim: Execute Queue synchronizes queued frame-synchronized commands at the next video vertical event or internally processed command-mode tearing event.
qualification: Multi-driver synchronization details are outside the specification; this does not identify the physical source of a received stripe.

claim: The supplied DSI PDF contains a CRC example comment with an x^15 term, while section 9.6 and Figure 49 specify x^12 and the example constant is 0x8408.

evidence.locator: PDF 100-101 / printed 88-89 and Annex B PDF 112 / printed 100 line 2516; both figures/code page visually checked

qualification: An internal inconsistency, not an official erratum. Implementation should follow a verified normative rule and independent test vectors, not copy the comment.

claim: The one-pixel 30-bit and 36-bit packet examples in the supplied PDF show a Word Count field of one although four or five payload bytes are displayed.

evidence.locator: PDF 71-72 / printed 59-60, lines 1575-1579 and 1597-1600; visual comparison with Word Count definition

qualification: Possible editorial inconsistency. No corrected packet hex sequence is asserted here; validate before use as decoder/encoder test vectors.

claim: The Arasan D-PHY PPI byte clock is specified as one eighth of HS bit rate; its 2.5-Gbit/s diagrams show a 1.25-GHz forwarded clock and 312.5-MHz byte clock.

evidence.locator: PDF 11-12,18-19 diagrams and PDF 30 / printed 24 Table 5

qualification: Illustrative vendor configuration, not A7 measurements. One label on PDF 11 has an extra decimal point; cross-checked against Table 5 and receiver diagrams.

claim: The vendor PPI separates HS request, ready, data-valid and receive-active/sync signals; a request edge triggers the PHY start/end sequence.
qualification: PPI control describes internal interface behavior. It is not an RF demodulation decision rule and gives no phone-specific register map.

claim: The Arasan combo PHY exposes periodic deskew-burst request and receive-calibration status signals.

evidence.locator: PDF 38 / printed 32, TxSkewCalHS and RxSkewCalHS rows visually reviewed

qualification: Calibration bursts are a candidate non-image activity class, not evidence that A7 or existing captures contain them.

claim: Arasan describes low-swing HS and larger single-ended LP signaling; these on-wire voltage swings do not by themselves determine the AM or PM index measured by an antenna.
qualification: The modulation-index conclusion is physical reasoning. Radiation channel, carrier reference, geometry and state mixture need measurement.

claim: The vendor Escape-mode received clock is generated from LP signaling and may be aperiodic.

evidence.locator: PDF 36 and 50 / printed 30 and 44, RxClkEsc rows

qualification: Do not force all LP control intervals into a constant-period HS model.

claim: The described C-PHY maps 16 PPI bits to seven symbols on a three-wire trio, whereas the described D-PHY uses a forwarded DDR clock.

evidence.locator: PDF 25-27 / printed 19-21; PDF 26 and 27 visually reviewed

qualification: C-PHY coding and clock relations are not used to infer the present D-PHY devices. Vendor document C-PHY revision labels vary and must be checked before a hardware implementation.

claim: Classic forwarded-clock DSI/D-PHY HS serialization uses 8 bits per byte and two bits per forwarded clock cycle; generic 8b/10b ×1.25 factor in vendor guide is invalid.
locator: Guide Driver Flow/Initialize DSI Bus; DSI lane and packet serialization sections

claim: Guide's0x84 ULPS statement is wrong. ACK time-order00100001 converts LSB-first to0x84; ULPS00011110 converts to0x78; TE01011101 converts to0xBA.
Host-to-peripheral DT0x16=Execute Queue;0x37=Set Maximum Return Packet Size. DCS read responses reverse direction are0x21,0x22,0x1C.
Guide short/long timing figures use ESC→0x87 and demonstrate LPDT, not HS DDR timing. They cannot supply HS bit/byte clock measurements.
locator: Short Packet Timing and Long Packet Timing figures

claim: UI_INST2–12.5ns implies80–500Mbps, not20–500Mbps in source prose.
locator: Common Issues lane bit rate range;figure10

claim: Four source headers have matching ECC, and two source payloads have matching CRC in MATLAB R2026b; two independent header reference vectors also pass.
limitation: No measured phone IQ packet decode.

claim: Guide's initialization snippet omits dbi_config, callback edata uses callback-list type instead of event-data type, and use_dma2d/refresh callback require API-version review.
RGB666 loosely packed DT0x2E transmits3bytes/pixel with useful bits[7:2]; ignored[1:0] not necessarily zero. Packed DT0x1E sends4pixels/9bytes. Color expansion EPF figure is not lane wire mapping.
